stem.en: Why would a donor place money with a guild, rather than hand it all to the monks to spend?

text.en: Because a guild was bound by law to spend the money on temples.
Because a guild could hold the money and pay fixed interest, so the income went on for years.
Because monks were not allowed to receive any gifts from a donor.
Because guild courts ordered every rich person to make a deposit.

explanation.en: The Nāśhik inscription shows guilds obligated to pay a fixed rate of interest on deposits, and the interest went to the Saṁgha. The deposit itself stayed in place, so the income could continue. That is what a perpetual endowment means. Monks did receive gifts, since the same donor gave them the cave.

hints.en: Think of what happens to money that is spent, and to money that earns interest.
